title: Universal cocomplete tensor of monoidal infinity categories
statement: Use the universe and monoidal infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $V,W$ be cocomplete monoidal infinity categories whose tensors preserve small colimits separately. Their cocomplete tensor product $V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W$ exists and is cocomplete, with a monoidal structure whose tensor preserves small colimits separately, and a strong monoidal functor $\mu:V\times W\to V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W$. For every cocomplete infinity category $Z$, restriction along $\mu$ gives an equivalence between the infinity category of colimit-preserving functors $V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W\to Z$ and that of functors $V\times W\to Z$ preserving colimits separately. If $Z$ is monoidal with separately cocontinuous tensor, this equivalence restricts to strong monoidal functors on both sides. In particular any separately cocontinuous strong monoidal $b:V\times W\to Z$ has a strong monoidal colimit-preserving factor $\bar b:V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W\to Z$ with a coherent monoidal equivalence $b\simeq\bar b\mu$. For presentably monoidal $V,W$, this tensor product is their tensor product as presentable categories and is presentably monoidal. Universes may be enlarged to contain these categories; the colimits in this assertion always refer to the fixed smaller universe.

source.place: Observation 3.9 and the following paragraph; section 8; Higher Algebra section 4.8.1 (cocomplete tensor universal property); online source, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $C=V\times W$. Let $R$ consist of all cocones $(p,w):K^{\triangleright}\to C$ with $p$ a small colimiting cocone in $V$ and $w\in W$ fixed, and all $(v,q)$ with $q$ a small colimiting cocone in $W$ and $v\in V$ fixed. Include $K=\varnothing$. These need not be colimiting cocones of the product $C$; they are prescribed relations. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] to this $C,R$, and define $T=P_R(C)$ and $\mu=j_R$. The category $T$ is cocomplete. Since $j_R$ sends these prescribed cocones to colimiting cocones, $\mu$ preserves small colimits separately. The set of small shapes and the collection $R$ fit in an enlarged ambient universe; the cited theorem keeps the colimit shapes in the original smaller universe.

source.place: Notation 4.8.1.7 and proof of Proposition 4.8.1.3; Variant 4.8.1.11 Online source, not archived; argument written out here.

proof.text: For any cocomplete $Z$, the unary equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] identifies $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(T,Z)$ with $\operatorname{Fun}_R(V\times W,Z)$ by restriction along $\mu$. A functor lies in the latter full category exactly when, for each fixed $w$, it preserves every small colimiting cocone in $V$, and, for each fixed $v$, every such cocone in $W$. This is exactly separate cocontinuity, on objects, transformations and all higher simplices. Thus this equivalence is the required unstructured universal property, without a presentability hypothesis on $Z$.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.1.3 (universal property); Haugseng Observation 3.9, paragraph following its first sentence Online source, not archived; argument written out here.

proof.text: Define $h:C\times C\to T$ by $h((v,w),(v',w'))=\mu(v\otimes_Vv',w\otimes_Ww')$. It sends $R$ to colimiting cocones in each $C$ variable: for instance a relation $(p,w)$ in the first variable is sent first to $(p\otimes_Vv',w\otimes_Ww')$, whose $V$ coordinate is a colimiting cocone because $-\otimes_Vv'$ preserves colimits, and then to a colimiting cocone by separate cocontinuity of $\mu$ from step 1. A relation $(v,q)$ uses $-\otimes_Ww'$ instead; relations in the second input use $v\otimes_V-$ and $w\otimes_W-$. The two-variable equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] therefore extends $h$ to a separately cocontinuous functor $m:T\times T\to T$, with a specified coherent equivalence $m(\mu(-),\mu(-))\simeq\mu((- )\otimes_C(-))$. Set the unit to $e=\mu(\mathbf1_V,\mathbf1_W)$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.8.1.3, using HTT Proposition 5.3.6.11; Remark 4.8.1.9 Online source, not archived; argument written out here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] with its small universe chosen large enough to contain $V,W,C,T$ and the total spaces of the fibrations (and with a still larger outer universe). This changes only the size bound for straightening; colimit shapes remain in the original $\mathcal U$. Use [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence] to write the given monoidal fibrations and their coherent transport as unital planar operation systems on $V$, $W$, and the product $C$, including the projection-pullback normal form for every block and tree. For each reduced ordered input list of length $r>0$ define $h_r:C^r\to T$ by $((v_i,w_i))\mapsto\mu(\bigotimes_i v_i,\bigotimes_i w_i)$, and use $e=\mu(\mathbf1_V,\mathbf1_W)$ at $r=0$. The calculation in step 3 shows that each $h_r$ sends every relation in $R$ to a colimiting cocone in each used variable. The finite-variable equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] therefore give separately cocontinuous operations $M_r:T^r\to T$ and coherent restriction equivalences $M_r\mu^r\simeq\mu h_r$. Apply [lem-coef-relative-planar-operation-extension] to lift the complete reduced-input substitution, unit, and higher tree simplices from the product operation system on $C$ to the $M_r$; this supplies all coherence before any unused variables are added. Pull those coherences back along the coordinate projections and use [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence] to assemble the full $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ diagram with value $T^n$, block operations $M_r$, empty blocks $e$, and inert projections. The resulting diagrams have Segal product equivalences because the inert maps are the coordinate projections. Unstraightening by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] gives a cocartesian fibration $p:T^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$. For $D\in T^m$, $Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)\in T^n$ and $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, the cocartesian mapping-space criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies $\operatorname{Map}^\phi(D,Y)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{T^n}(\phi_!D,Y)$, which is $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_T((\phi_!D)_i,Y_i)$; each factor is $\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}(D,Y_i)$ by the same criterion. Thus composition with inert projections is an equivalence, including the contractible empty product for $n=0$, so [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] applies. The coherent maps $\mu^n:C^n\to T^n$ preserve the lifted operations and projections, hence [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence] makes them a strong monoidal functor; its binary operation is $m$ from step 3.

source.place: Remark 4.8.1.9 and Proposition 4.8.1.10; aritywise coherent extension as in proof of Proposition 4.8.1.3 Online source, not archived; argument written out here. For the cocartesian-fibration model, HTT Theorem 3.2.0.1 with Proposition 4.2.4.4, cocartesian dual, as stated in lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening.

proof.text: Let $Z$ be monoidal with separately cocontinuous tensor, and let $b:C\to Z$ be separately cocontinuous and strong monoidal. Step 2 gives a colimit-preserving extension $\bar b:T\to Z$ and a coherent equivalence $\bar b\mu\simeq b$. The $n$-fold tensor comparison for $\bar b$ is a comparison between separately cocontinuous functors $T^n\to Z$: one is $\bar b$ applied to $M_n$, and the other is the $n$-fold tensor of $\bar b$ in $Z$. Their restrictions to $C^n$ are the specified operation comparisons of the strong monoidal $b$. Apply [lem-coef-strong-monoidal-operation-morphism-lifting] together with [lem-coef-relative-planar-operation-extension]. Its operation-system classification identifies strong monoidal functors with coherent planar-operation morphisms, and its relative lifting clause lifts these comparisons, their inverses, the unit comparison at arity zero, and every substitution and higher compatibility simplex. The same full-faithfulness statement lifts transformations and all higher mapping-space simplices, so restriction is an equivalence of the infinity categories of strong monoidal functors, not merely a bijection on equivalence classes. Conversely restriction of a strong monoidal colimit-preserving $\bar b$ is separately cocontinuous and strong monoidal, and the lifted comparison restricts to the original $b$.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.1.10 (structured universal property); Remark 4.8.1.9 Online source, not archived; argument written out here.

proof.text: Suppose $V,W$ are presentable. Choose the small presentations $i:A\to V$, $j:B\to W$ and small families $R_A,R_B$ of bounded colimit relations supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-bounded-colimit-presentation]. Let $R_{AB}$ consist of $(r,b)$ for $r\in R_A,b\in B$ and $(a,s)$ for $a\in A,s\in R_B$. The category $A\times B$ and this family are small; hence $Q=P_{R_{AB}}(A\times B)$ is presentable by the small-data clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion]. Its generator functor respects $R_A,R_B$ separately, so the finite-variable clause of that node, using $P_{R_A}(A)\simeq V$ and $P_{R_B}(B)\simeq W$, extends it to a separately cocontinuous $V\times W\to Q$. Step 2 factors this through a cocontinuous $f:T\to Q$. Conversely $\mu(i(-),j(-))$ respects $R_{AB}$ and gives a cocontinuous $g:Q\to T$. The restrictions of $fg$ and $\mathrm{id}_Q$ to $A\times B$ agree; the unary universal property for $Q$ makes them equivalent. The restrictions of $gf\mu$ and $\mu$ to $A\times B$ agree; finite-variable full faithfulness for the two small presentations first makes them equivalent on $V\times W$, and step 2 then gives $gf\simeq\mathrm{id}_T$. Thus $T\simeq Q$ is presentable. Its universal property from step 2, restricted to presentable targets, is the defining bilinear universal property of the tensor of presentable categories, which identifies $T$ with that tensor. By [def-coef-complete-algebroid], presentability of $T$ together with separate cocontinuity of $m$ is exactly presentable monoidality. The small presentations show this is presentability in the original universe, not merely in the enlarged ambient one.
